package_info.why_malicious: The package was published by an unknown actor who took over an abandoned package name and inserted code designed to exfiltrate sensitive user and host information to attacker-controlled domains. This is a clear supply chain attack leveraging trust in open-source dependencies.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects local user, hostname, and environment variable data, then sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in credential and environment exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive information to an external domain without user consent or legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not send local environment or user data to external servers during import or installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or crash reporting (with user consent and clear documentation).
key_indicators: Hardcoded external domains (oast.fun, burpcollaborator.net, pipedream.net, webhook.site)
Collection of environment variables and user/host info

attack_chain.action: Attacker claims abandoned package name and publishes a new version containing malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to unsuspecting users via dependency updates.

attack_chain.action: When the package is installed or imported, the malicious code executes, collecting sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled domains via HTTPS POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive information from victim systems.

behavioral_signatures: Network requests to suspicious or hardcoded domains during install/import
Access to process.env, os.userInfo(), or os.hostname() in package entry points
Unexpected data exfiltration in open-source packages
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing network exfiltration logic
References to oast.fun, burpcollaborator.net, pipedream.net, webhook.site
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for open-source packages that make network requests to known suspicious domains (such as oast.fun, burpcollaborator.net, pipedream.net, webhook.site) during installation or import. Flag packages that access sensitive environment variables or user/host information and transmit them externally. Use static analysis to detect hardcoded domain names and dynamic analysis to observe unexpected network activity during package installation or first use.
